newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end up after posting 8-1/2 year high.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end up after posting 8-1/2 year high.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended firmer on Wednesday after setting 8-1/2 year highs on ideas dry weather may cut output in Brazil and on news a nationwide Brazilian port strike was called for Friday, traders said.
But soybeans faltered late in the session amid reports Brazil's key Paranagua port would not take part in the strike.

"There will be some strikes in Brazil," said Bob Lekberg, analyst with Goldenberg-Hehmeyer. "Whether that impacts the port of Paranagua is uncertain but that was still a sustaining factor. We also had rumors that China had bought a Panamax cargo of (U.S.) soybeans but that was hard to confirm."
U.S. exporters could not confirm the Chinese purchase. But they noted shipping delays out of Brazil and said if China needed soybeans quickly, they would have to buy U.S. supplies.

Soybeans were further bolstered by news soybean production in Brazil's Rio Grande do Sul could fall to 5.25 million tonnes from an earlier estimate of 5.68 million, according to a division of the state's agricultural secretariat.

Soybeans ended 9-1/4 to three cents per bushel higher with may up eight at $8.83-1/2. The new high for the May is $8.88, topping the previous high of $8.85-3/4 set on Tuesday and the highest level for a nearby contract since September 1988.

"We have very localized information indicating there is damage to the crop due to dryness," said Carlos Cardosa, economist at Emater, which provides technical assistance to farmers. "That would cause a drop in productivity to 1,800 kilos per hectare which is a preliminary estimate."
He added that final production estimates would not be available until next week but said "the reduction is not going to be less than five percent."
Futures gains were limited by active farmer selling.
"We saw some producer selling and some easing of basis bids throughout the Midwest and Gulf today," Lekberg said.
The July/November spread narrowed in early trade amid unwinding of bull spreads but tacked on 3-1/4 cents on the close. The spread settled at $1.86-3/4. premium July.
On the day, Smith Barney bought three million bushels November and 1.5 million May, traders said, and Griffin Trading bought two million July and one million May.
Refco Inc spread one million bushels July/November at $1.84 to $1.87, premium July, while Lee B. Stern spread 1.5 million November/July at $1.80, floor sources said.
In options trade, Tradelink bought 750 July $8.75 calls and sold 750 July $8.25 calls at 26 cents.
Tradelink also bought 400 November $7.25 calls and sold 400 November $8.00 calls at 16-1/2 cents, traders said.
Soybean volume was estimated by CBOT at 75,000 contracts, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 69,064 contracts.
